newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta's premier hints at surplus over C$2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Alberta's premier hints at surplus over C$2 bln.

text.p: Ralph Klein, premier of the oil-rich Canadian province of Alberta, hinted strongly in an interview that his government would ring up a 1996-97 budget surplus of over C$2 billion.

Klein, in a year-end interview with Reuters, said continued higher-than-budgeted energy revenues thanks to strong oil prices could drive Alberta's surplus beyond the last official target of C$1.7 billion.
"Things are holding -- you just have to do the math. There's no indication, believe it or not, that the (oil and gas) prices are going to crash," Klein said.
"When you're budgeted at US$18 (per barrel oil) and it goes up to US$24, falls back to US$22 or US$20, you're still cushioned."
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude oil has traded above US$26 per barrel in the last week, its highest level since the Gulf War.
To help attract business, a main plank of the strategy would be to keep corporate taxes low, Klein said.
"As a matter of policy, we must maintain the most competitive tax regime in the country and work towards a tax regime that is comparable to some of the most competitive American states," he said.

Klein said he planned no "radical departures" from his government's tight-fisted fiscal policies, which, since his Conservative Party was elected in 1993, has eliminated a C$3-billion deficit, paid down the public debt by C$4 billion and brought down three consecutive surplus budgets.
